chapters.content:
## Institutional Corrections

Study the following concepts and review items related to Institutional Corrections. Understanding these concepts is essential for passing the criminology board examination.

### Important Points to Remember:

- Imprisonment serves both as punishment for crimes and as an opportunity for rehabilitation
- The Bureau of Corrections (BUCOR) manages national penitentiaries for those sentenced to more than 3 years
- BJMP manages city, district, and municipal jails for those awaiting trial or serving sentences of 3 years or less
- Jails hold those awaiting trial or short sentences; prisons hold those with longer sentences
- New Bilibid Prison is the national penitentiary located in Muntinlupa City
- Medium security prisons house inmates with moderate security risks
- Minimum security prisons house low-risk inmates, often those nearing release
- A prison is a facility where convicted criminals serve their sentences

## Non-Institutional Corrections

Study the following concepts and review items related to Non-Institutional Corrections. Understanding these concepts is essential for passing the criminology board examination.

### Important Points to Remember:

- Probation is a court-ordered period of supervision in the community as an alternative to imprisonment
- The Parole and Probation Administration supervises probationers and parolees in the community
- PD 968 is the Probation Law of 1976, establishing the probation system in the Philippines
- The trial court that convicted the offender has the power to grant probation
- Offenders sentenced to more than 6 years imprisonment are not eligible for probation
- Probation allows offenders to serve their sentence in the community under supervision
- Parole is the conditional release of a prisoner before completing their sentence
- Parole is release after serving part of prison sentence; probation is instead of imprisonment

## Parole

Study the following concepts and review items related to Parole. Understanding these concepts is essential for passing the criminology board examination.

### Important Points to Remember:

- Parole is the conditional release of a prisoner before completing their full sentence
- The Indeterminate Sentence Law requires courts to impose minimum and maximum terms
- The Board of Pardons and Parole grants parole to qualified prisoners
- The Board of Pardons and Parole supervises and grants parole
- Parole supervision monitors released inmates compliance with conditions
- New crimes or violating conditions results in parole revocation
- Mandatory release occurs when inmates serve required portion of sentence
- Indeterminate sentences have a range allowing parole consideration

## Rehabilitation Programs

Study the following concepts and review items related to Rehabilitation Programs. Understanding these concepts is essential for passing the criminology board examination.

### Important Points to Remember:

- Rehabilitation aims to reform offenders and help them reintegrate into society as law-abiding citizens
- GCTA is time credited to inmates for good conduct, reducing their prison stay
- Livelihood programs teach inmates skills for employment after release
- Restorative justice focuses on repairing harm through cooperation between offenders and victims
- Rehabilitation aims to reform offenders so they can successfully reintegrate into society
- Vocational training teaches inmates practical job skills for employment after release
- Behavior modification uses structured programs to change inmate behavior
- Work release allows inmates to work outside prison during the day

## Inmate Classification

Study the following concepts and review items related to Inmate Classification. Understanding these concepts is essential for passing the criminology board examination.

### Important Points to Remember:

- Inmates are classified based on security risk and needs for appropriate placement and programming
- Reception and diagnostic centers assess new inmates for proper classification and placement
- Classification considers crime committed, length of sentence, behavior, and security risk
- Classification ensures inmates are placed appropriately based on security and treatment needs
- Maximum security is for the most dangerous inmates requiring highest supervision
- Minimum security is for low-risk inmates who need minimal supervision
- Reclassification periodically reviews inmate security level based on behavior and progress
- Reception centers assess new inmates for proper classification and placement

chapters.introduction: This chapter covers Prison Security with 14 review items essential for the board examination.
chapters.content:
## Prison Security

Study the following concepts and review items related to Prison Security. Understanding these concepts is essential for passing the criminology board examination.

### Important Points to Remember:

- Maximum security prisons house the most dangerous criminals who pose the highest escape or violence risk
- Contraband refers to items prohibited inside prison, such as weapons, drugs, and phones
- Solitary confinement isolates an inmate from the general prison population
- Philippine prisons have maximum, medium, and minimum security classifications
- A lockdown confines all inmates to their cells during emergencies or security threats
- Supermax prisons have the highest security level for the most dangerous inmates
- Contraband refers to any item prohibited within prison facilities
- Shakedowns are unannounced searches for prohibited items

## Therapeutic Communities

Study the following concepts and review items related to Therapeutic Communities. Understanding these concepts is essential for passing the criminology board examination.

### Important Points to Remember:

- A therapeutic community is a residential treatment program focusing on substance abuse and behavioral change
- A therapeutic community is a treatment environment focused on behavioral change and rehabilitation
- Therapeutic Community model creates a structured environment promoting behavioral change
- Therapeutic communities use peer support for drug rehabilitation
- The 12-step program is a structured recovery approach for addiction
- Therapeutic milieu uses the entire environment for rehabilitation
- Encounter groups use peer confrontation to address negative behaviors
- Therapeutic communities use group-based treatment and peer support for rehabilitation

chapters.content:
## Pardon and Amnesty

Study the following concepts and review items related to Pardon and Amnesty. Understanding these concepts is essential for passing the criminology board examination.

### Important Points to Remember:

- The President of the Philippines has the power to grant pardons, reprieves, and amnesty
- Pardon is granted to individuals after conviction; amnesty is for groups, often political offenders
- Commutation is the reduction of a sentence to a lesser penalty
- Reprieve is a temporary postponement or suspension of the execution of a sentence
- Pardon is an act of executive clemency that forgives the offense and its consequences
- Amnesty is a general pardon granted to a group, usually for political offenses
- Commutation reduces the penalty imposed without forgiving the offense
- Pardon is granted to individuals; amnesty is a general pardon to groups, usually for political offenses
